Keep the other trusted host entry while correcting the target host record.
scenarios.explanation: The trusted host record identifies the supplied server; the separate authorized-key file controls which client identity can use its account. Keeping these roles separate restores the intended modeled access.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the failing stage, change the relevant document or attributes, save it, apply policy if changed, then Check access again.
scenarios.simplifications: Supplied, reachable server and public client identities are exercise assumptions. No SSH process, private key, network, signature/encryption verification or real login is used. Plain Ed25519 public encodings, literal lower-case host/IPv4 trust, supported sshd_config directives and ordinary nonroot /home/USER key paths only. No agent, key generation, PAM/ACL/SELinux, Match/Include, hashed/wildcard hosts, forwarding, certificates or general SSH utility conformance. Unsupported behavior is not counted as a denied request.
